ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of the semicircle $O$, and $\angle BAC=28^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect CB, \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of the semicircle O, and $\angle BAC=28^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle B=\angle ACB - \angle BAC=90^\circ - 28^\circ = 62^\circ$, \\
Also, $\because$ quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in the circle, \\
$\therefore \angle D + \angle ABC= 180^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle D=180^\circ - 62^\circ = \boxed{118^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an upper semicircle with AB as diameter, A is at the left endpoint, B is at the right endpoint, and O is marked as the center on AB; D is located above and slightly to the left on the semicircular arc, and C is located on the right-side circular arc. AD, DC, and AC are connected in the figure, and the required ∠D is the angle formed by DA and DC, namely ∠ADC. The problem gives ∠BAC=28°. Reasoning: According to the positions in the figure, A, D, C, and B are all on the same circle, and AB is the diameter. ∠BAC is an inscribed angle, and the arc it intercepts is arc BC, so the measure of arc BC is 2×28°=56°. Because AB is the diameter, the lower semicircular arc AB in the complete circle that does not pass through the upper semicircle is 180°. ∠ADC intercepts the arc AC that does not contain D; this arc can be regarded as the lower semicircular arc AB plus arc BC, therefore arc AC=180°+56°=236°. An inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of its intercepted arc, so ∠ADC=236°÷2=118°. Therefore ∠D=118°.
